samples.summary: Vacuous assertion in the new read-only getStore() test: `expect(editor.getPageSetup()).toEqual(before)` passes whether or not the read-only guard works
samples.evidence: `Doc` caches the document (`packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:105,123` — `_document` is only refreshed by `refresh()`), and `editor.getPageSetup()` reads `resolvePageSetup(doc.document.pageSetup)` (editor.ts:3047). `guardedSetPageSetup` (editor.ts:2888-2898) writes only to `docStore` and deliberately does not call `doc.refresh()`. So even if the `if (readOnly) return;` line were deleted, the write would land in the store and `editor.getPageSetup()` would still return `before` — this assertion cannot fail on the behavior it claims to cover. Only the following line (`editor.getStore().getDocument().pageSetup` is undefined) actually exercises the guard; the first assertion is decoration presented as coverage.

samples.summary: No test covers the proxy's `set` trap, which is the anti-bypass half of the new guard
samples.evidence: editor.ts:2910-2914 adds a `set` trap that returns `false` for `setPageSetup` ("Assigning over the guard would be a way around it"), which in strict mode makes `editor.getStore().setPageSetup = fn` throw a TypeError. Neither new test, nor any other docs test, assigns to a member of the store returned by `getStore()`. If the trap regressed (e.g. someone dropped the `set` handler), every test here would still pass while the guard became bypassable with a one-line assignment that then persists a closed content box into the CRDT.
searchedFor: grep 'getStore()' across repo (only editor-page-setup.test.ts, editor-read-only.test.ts, frontend src)

samples.summary: Memoization-invalidation behavior the comment explicitly promises (a method replaced on the store — a test spy — is still picked up) is untested
samples.evidence: editor.ts:2884-2909 caches `{raw, bound}` per property and re-binds only when `raw` changes; the doc comment claims this keeps test spies working. The only related assertion is `expect(editor.getStore().canUndo).toBe(editor.getStore().canUndo)` (editor-page-setup.test.ts:349), which proves stable identity but would also pass for a non-memoized/no-proxy implementation of the stale-cache bug's opposite. No test replaces a store method (e.g. `store.canUndo = vi.fn()`) and asserts the guarded store returns the replacement, so a cache that never invalidates would ship green — silently breaking any future spy-based test or store that swaps methods at runtime.
searchedFor: grep 'vi.fn' near docs view tests via getStore search

samples.summary: The accepted-write half of the new test asserts only the store, never that the editor is left consistent (no doc.refresh, no repaint, no undo snapshot)
samples.evidence: editor-page-setup.test.ts:343-345 calls `editor.getStore().setPageSetup(accepted)` and asserts `store.getDocument().pageSetup?.margins.left === 72`. `guardedSetPageSetup` (editor.ts:2888-2898) intentionally skips `docStore.snapshot()`, `doc.refresh()`, `invalidateLayout()` and `render()` that `writePageSetup` (editor.ts:2078-2090) performs, so after this accepted write the editor still reports/renders the old page and the change is not on the undo stack. No test pins that documented consequence (e.g. asserting `editor.getPageSetup()` is unchanged, or the undo behavior), so a future change in either direction — refreshing, or accidentally clobbering the undo stack — is invisible to the suite.

samples.summary: No test that the guarded setter copies the caller's object (the `resolvePageSetup` copy-on-write claim in the comment)
samples.evidence: editor.ts:2891-2897 says `resolvePageSetup` copies on the way in "for the same reason `writePageSetup` does". `EditorAPI.setPageSetup` has a dedicated aliasing test (editor-page-setup.test.ts:144-157 'the caller keeps no alias into document state after a write'), but the new getStore() test has no counterpart. Coverage here is weak-but-contained because `MemDocStore.setPageSetup` deep-clones anyway (packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:99), so a real aliasing regression would only show against a store that keeps what it is handed (e.g. YorkieDocStore).
